authored.observedEffect: A current-run authenticated workbench watch classified the new source PURE_C and compiled a 824-byte, 206-instruction logical owner with no expected-only or actual-only instruction. Compared with retail, its symbolic object has zero opcode, branch-polarity, stack-offset, and memory-width/signedness mismatches; register-field differences fall from E41's historical 31 to 26 and aligned instruction differences from 52 to 47. The two 240-byte .rodata tables together have raw SHA-256 FA3509166739A476B9FE7D429B60665FC8BC54AA81746DC954A28314727A97DA, identical to E41 and the accepted fixture. All 120 auxiliary R_MIPS_32 records are identical to E41 after normalizing the compiler-adjusted text-section name. No production source, linkage, or full-ROM acceptance input changed.
authored.remainingFailure: The owner remains nonexact: 47 aligned symbolic instruction differences and 26 register-field differences remain; raw relocation-bearing addresses cannot be judged exact without approved ownership and a canonical linked diff. The outer owner/other and inner strongest/cursor/slot register-priority cycles remain. This source is the best recoverable pure-C research candidate, not matching C. B894's separate structural activation still needs Astra approval; W5's eight-member final verifier remains pending.
